plans.note: Cap is mutual at greater of 12 months' Fees or USD 1,000,000 (21.1) with consequential-damages exclusion (21.2) and Excluded Claims definition (21.3). Check that Excluded Claims covers Vendor IP indemnity/third-party claims given the missing indemnity section, and confirm 21.4 savings language.

No Section 20 (indemnification) appears in the outline even though 9.3 cross-references 'Section 20.5' and 21.3 assumes 'indemnification obligations' exist. Propose inserting a Vendor indemnity (third-party IP, confidentiality/privacy/security, personal injury, law violations) with defence/control mechanics, and keep any Customer indemnity narrow.

Duplicate-numbered 12.4 imposes a 24-month, all-territory non-compete on Customer, which we reject outright and which directly contradicts the freedom-of-action acknowledgement in 12.3. Delete and rely on 12.3.

Section 7.2 (first instance) functions as a right of first refusal before engaging another provider, and 2.1's take-or-pay reinforces de facto exclusivity; both conflict with the no-exclusivity acknowledgement in 12.3. Strike 7.2 first instance.

Section 7.2 (first instance) is a reverse MFN obliging us to disclose and match third-party offers — wrong direction; delete, consistent with 12.3's no most-favoured-customer commitment. Note the duplicate 7.2 numbering (invoicing clause at sec-7.2-2) when redlining.

Section 12.4 is a one-way 24-month no-hire with no general-advertising carve-out ('regardless of how the employee applies'); narrow to 12 months, mutual, solicitation only, with carve-outs for general recruitment — as 12.3 already contemplates.

Section 9 jumps from 9.3 to 9.5, and no convenience-termination right appears; 2.1 expressly denies termination rights. Add a Customer-only termination for convenience on 30–60 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and confirm Vendor has no reciprocal walk-away.

8.2 gives a 30-day non-renewal window plus a 60-day reminder with deadline extension, and 8.3 caps uplift at lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice — largely compliant; verify the reminder/opt-out mechanics are workable and that no increase touches prepaid periods.

28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts while 28.2 gives exclusive jurisdiction to New York courts — a direct conflict. Delete 28.1 or replace with New York governing law to align with 28.2; 28.3's escalation is acceptable.

24.1 permits our Affiliate/successor assignment, 24.2 restricts Vendor, and 24.4 blocks repricing or termination on our change of control — aligned; cross-check licence transferability in 13.3 and that 24.3 does not override 24.1.

14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of Deliverables created for us with only a revocable, non-transferable term licence — reverse to Customer ownership (or at minimum a perpetual, irrevocable, transferable licence per 13.2). 14.1/14.4 on Customer Data and feedback are acceptable.

13.1–13.2 cover Affiliates and contractors and grant a perpetual paid-up licence, and 13.3 limits revocation; the outlier is 14.2's revocable, non-transferable Deliverable licence, which must be conformed.

22.1–22.3 already limit audits to once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, at Vendor's cost absent a >5% shortfall, with confidentiality — confirm no broader access rights elsewhere (e.g., Section 23 records).

No express liquidated damages or penalty payable by Customer appears; the closest exposure is the unconditional take-or-pay in 2.1 (shortfall effectively a penalty). Also confirm service credits run in our favour — 1.5 excludes credits from Fees but no SLA credit clause is in the outline.

19.1–19.3 give services, conformity, malicious-code and compliance warranties; 19.2's 90-day Deliverable window is short (seek 12 months) and 19.4's repair/refund remedy should remain non-exclusive as drafted. Check 19.5 disclaimer does not undercut 19.1–19.3.

Coverage lines and limits are present (18.1) with certificates and non-limitation language (18.2); confirm cyber limit is adequate for the data volumes and that additional-insured/notice terms suffice.

2.1 imposes a USD 2M/year three-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights, contradicting 12.3's no-minimum-volume acknowledgement; delete or convert to a non-binding forecast with rollover credits and an exit right.

Section 10 addresses access cut-off, Deliverable delivery and refunds but contains no transition-assistance obligation or Customer Data return/export in a usable format; note 16.5 cross-references a Section 11 that is not in the outline. Add exit assistance at agreed rates plus data extraction and certified deletion.
